After coming back from my college Algorithm exam today, I didn't feel like solving another DSA problem.
Instead, I wanted to understand something that powers real distributed systems.
So I picked up a concept from System Design: Distributed Locking.
Interestingly, many subjects I'm studying started connecting together.
While reading Cache Memory in Computer Organization & Architecture, I explored how Redis stores data in memory and why it's so fast.
While studying Deadlocks in Operating Systems, I understood why distributed systems need lock expiration (TTL) to prevent resources from being blocked forever.
While learning about atomic operations, I implemented Redis' SET NX PX command and used a Lua script for safe lock release.
Instead of only reading about the concept, I built it from scratch.

What I implemented :-
Redis-based Distributed Lock
Atomic lock acquisition using SET NX PX
UUID-based lock ownership
Automatic lock expiration (TTL)
Safe lock release using Lua scripting
Docker-based Redis setup
Detailed documentation with architecture diagrams

Building it helped me understand why distributed locking exists, not just how it works.
One thing I've started enjoying is connecting concepts across subjects.
Reading about cache in COA and applying it through Redis.
Reading about deadlocks in Operating Systems and seeing the same problem solved in System Design.
Those moments make me feel like I'm gradually thinking more like an engineer than someone who is only solving interview questions.

Repository:
 https://lnkd.in/dCCNMjS3

I'm planning to continue exploring one system design concept at a time and implementing each from scratch.
Feedback and suggestions are always welcome.
